ai.title: Replace native confirm with custom ConfirmationDialog
ai.summary: Native `window.confirm` calls replaced with custom `ConfirmationDialog` component in API key management. This change addresses poor UI consistency and lack of styling control by implementing a reusable dialog component. Scope covers `web/src/components/ui/confirmation-dialog.tsx` (new) and `web/src/app/profile/components/api-keys-section.tsx`. The new component supports configurable title, description, confirm text, destructive variant, and processing state.

eli5.text: When you go to revoke an API key in your profile, you'll now see a styled pop-up dialog instead of the browser's plain default alert. The new dialog lets the team match the look of the rest of the app and shows a clear message, a cancel button, and a confirm button that can show a loading state while the revocation happens. This replaces the old browser-native confirm window that looked out of place in the settings page.

ai.title: Standardize session type handling in web profile
ai.summary: Refactored `web/src/app/api/user/sessions/route.ts` to filter PATs via DB query instead of runtime loop, and updated `sessionType` to return raw DB value. Modified `web/src/app/profile/components/security-section.tsx` to expect 'web'/'cli' types and memoized session filtering. Added `deleteSessions` helper and `Session` type definition.

eli5.text: When you open your account's security page to review your active login sessions, the list now correctly separates your web browser sessions from your command-line/CLI tool sessions and no longer tries to hide or mislabel the personal access tokens used by those tools in the background. Behind the scenes, the server now asks the database directly to exclude the tool-related tokens instead of fetching everything and filtering it in the application code, and the labels shown to you now come straight from what the database already stores rather than being translated on the fly. If you looked, you'd see browser sessions displayed under a dedicated section with a monitor icon and command-line sessions under a separate section with a terminal icon, and the page loads the same sessions as before

ai.title: Add initCommand to git evals
ai.summary: Adds optional `initCommand` to `EvalData` and `setupTestRepo` to execute repo-specific setup commands like `bun install` during eval scaffolding. `run-git-evals.ts` and `run-single-eval.ts` pass this command through to the setup function. `setup-test-repo.ts` implements execution via `execFileSync` with a 240s timeout and error handling. Scope limited to internal evals in `evals/git-evals/`.

eli5.text: The internal evaluation system can now run a setup step, like installing dependencies, when preparing a test repository for an eval run. If you look at the eval configuration, you will see a new optional field that specifies a command to run right after the repository is cloned and checked out at the right commit. This only affects internal evals in the git evals folder and is already live today.

ai.title: Backend error logging and agent step validation
ai.summary: Added debug logging to `mainPrompt` and enhanced error reporting in `runProgrammaticStep` and `websocket-action`. `runProgrammaticStep` now validates tool availability against agent templates and logs structured error objects, while `websocket-action` uses `getErrorObject` for consistent logging.

eli5.text: When the assistant runs an automated step, it now checks that the tool being requested is actually allowed for that specific agent, throwing a clear error if it isn't. Debug-level logging was added when the assistant finishes building its main prompt, recording the resulting state for easier troubleshooting. Across the three affected files, error reporting was made more consistent by routing details through a shared helper and by formatting error messages as plain text instead of nested objects. No direct behavior changes surface for end users; these are behind-the-scenes improvements that make failures easier to diagnose. The changes are live today as part of the 2025-08-23 snapshot.

ai.title: Scout agent model switch to Flash 2.5
ai.summary: Scout agent model changed from gemini-2.5-pro to gemini-2.5-flash. Reasoning options removed. System prompt clarified to read-only capacity. Instructions updated to enforce thinking tags and parallel agent spawning. Researcher and file-explorer prompts refined for clarity.

eli5.text: The assistant that helps find answers now uses a faster, simpler model instead of the more thorough one, so it responds more quickly at the cost of deep reasoning. Its instructions now explicitly tell it to stay read-only and never edit files, and it is guided to gather information by launching multiple helper agents at once and wrapping thoughts in special tags. If you asked it a question and looked at its process, you would see it spawn parallel helpers for web and codebase searches rather than reasoning at length before acting.

ai.title: fix: auto-topup occasional test failures due to missing mock
ai.summary: Added mock for `@codebuff/common/util/logger` in `backend/src/__tests__/auto-topup.test.ts` to resolve occasional test failures. The `beforeEach` block now stubs `logger` methods and `withLoggerContext` to prevent undefined references during auto-topup execution.

eli5.text: Some of the background checks the system runs before upgrading accounts were randomly crashing for a small number of internal tests, so the team added a fake logging helper to those checks. This doesn't change anything you see in your account right now, but it makes those internal tests run consistently instead of flaking out unpredictably.

ai.title: Subagent cost aggregation tracks credits in agent state
ai.summary: Agent state now includes `creditsUsed` field, initialized to 0 in `createAgentState` and `spawn-agent-inline`. `saveMessage` returns `creditsUsed` number instead of void/null. `promptAiSdkStream`/`promptAiSdk`/`promptAiSdkStructured` accept optional `onCostCalculated` callback, invoked after `saveMessage` resolves. `runAgentStep` passes callback to accumulate costs into `agentState.creditsUsed`. `handleSpawnAgents` aggregates `creditsUsed` from fulfilled and failed subagent results into parent state. Scope: backend agent execution and cost tracking subsystems.

eli5.text: The system now keeps a running tally of how much money each assistant session costs as it works, instead of only calculating costs at the very end. This only affects backend agent execution and cost tracking, so you wouldn't see a direct UI change, but the system can now report accumulated costs accurately for parent assistants that spawn subagents.

ai.title: Add web-researcher and docs-researcher agents
ai.summary: Introduced web-researcher and docs-researcher agents to the scout agent's spawnable list, enabling targeted web and technical documentation searches. These new agents use Google Gemini 2.5 Flash and are defined in `.agents/web-researcher.ts` and `.agents/docs-researcher.ts` with corresponding factories in `.agents/factory/`. The `read-docs` tool parameters were updated to make `topic` required and clarify library name expectations.

eli5.text: The software's research assistant can now send out two new specialized helpers on your behalf: one that browses the web for current information and another that reads technical documentation. These helpers were already available to be called but the main research coordinator now actively knows to use them and can launch as many of the web or documentation helpers as you need in a single request. If you asked the assistant to research something, you would notice it is now quicker to pull in up-to-date web results and official documentation alongside its normal file searching, and you may see it spawn multiple searchers at once instead of just one. The change was released today.

ai.title: Fix types in read-docs tool definition
ai.summary: Added `topic` parameter to MongoDB example in `backend/src/tools/definitions/tool/read-docs.ts`. This aligns the tool definition with the expected type signature, resolving type errors. Scope limited to backend tool definitions and associated tests.

eli5.text: The internal tool that the assistant uses to read documentation now provides a clearer instruction for looking up MongoDB setup help, including the specific topic it covers. This behind-the-scenes fix corrects how that lookup request is formatted so it matches what the system expects, and it keeps the related automated checks in sync. You won't see any visible change in the assistant's responses; the correction prevents type-validation failures that could otherwise cause that documentation lookup to break during development.

ai.title: readdocs maxtokens default 20000
ai.summary: read_docs max_tokens default raised 10k to 20k in common/src/tools/params/tool/read-docs.ts. Zod schema adds .default(20_000) before .optional(), updating describe text to match. Floor of 10k for lower values unchanged. Core tool params only.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to read a document, it now pulls in twice as much text by default instead of stopping at the old limit. So a longer portion of whatever file you point it at comes back to you in one go. The change only affects how much gets fetched unless you type in your own smaller number, in which case that smaller number still wins.

ai.summary: Step limit prompt in `.agents/base2/editor.ts` now directs agent to use `set_output` tool for progress summary, replacing generic summary request. Ensures structured output capture at step limit. Affects internal editor agent behavior.

eli5.text: When the assistant running inside the internal coding helper reaches its step limit, it now uses a specific tool to record its summary of progress, what's left to solve, and any insights to help finish the work. This replaces the previous behavior of asking for a generic summary. You wouldn't notice this directly as an end user, but if you looked at how the assistant behaves when it hits its working limit, you'd see it using the structured output tool instead of just producing free-form text.

ai.title: Per-subagent cost attribution
ai.summary: Backend tracks `agentId` in `message-cost-tracker` and `ai-sdk` streams. Client `subagent-storage` accumulates `creditsUsed` per agent via new `addCreditsByAgentId`. CLI `subagent-list` and `traces` render yellow credit counts for active subagents. `MessageCostResponseSchema` gains optional `agentId` field.

eli5.text: If you ask an assistant made up of multiple sub-agents, each sub-agent can now show you exactly how many credits it has spent. When a sub-agent runs, the system remembers which one it was, and the command-line tool that lists your sub-agents will display those per-agent credit counts next to each one. You would notice this when listing your sub-agents, the credit numbers appear in yellow, making the cost tracking clearer than before.

ai.title: Planner switches to gpt-5-high for complex tasks
ai.summary: Planner agent updated to use gpt-5-high model specifically for complex tasks. The `planner-gpt-5-high` definition is removed and replaced by a generic `planner` in `base2-gpt-5-high.ts`. `planner-factory.ts` now configures the planner with `structured_output`, adds `read_files`/`set_output` tools, and spawns `web-researcher`/`docs-researcher` instead of `gemini-thinker-high`. `docs-researcher.ts` spawner prompt clarified to target major public libraries/frameworks.

eli5.text: The planner now uses the GPT-5 High model exclusively for complex tasks, switching from a model that handled everything. If you triggered a plan, you'd notice it's labeled for heavyweight work and is slower because it's reserved for genuinely complex problems. This only affects the internal planning agent, not any direct user-facing feature yet.

ai.title: Scout and planner switch to openai/gpt-5-chat
ai.summary: Scout and planner agents now use openai/gpt-5-chat, replacing google/gemini-2.5-flash and google/gemini-2.5-pro respectively. The scout definition drops reasoningOptions (effort: 'low', exclude: true) as gpt-5-chat handles reasoning natively. Changes touch .agents/base2/scout.ts, .agents/base2/planner.ts, and common/src/templates/initial-agents-dir/types/agent-definition.ts where openai/gpt-5-chat is added to ModelName.

eli5.text: If you use the Scout and Planner agents (the AI helpers that explore and map out work in the base2 setup), they now talk to a different underlying AI model. Instead of using Google's Gemini models, both agents have switched to OpenAI's gpt-5-chat, which should be active today for anyone running those specific agents. This is behind-the-scenes glue work: the same helpers now send their questions to a different answer engine, with no change to what you see or how you use them.

ai.title: Scout gains readfiles, Editor filters successful edits
ai.summary: Scout agent (Lewis & Clark) gains read_files tool to directly inspect codebase files. System prompt reinforces read-only constraint, explicitly instructing not to offer code changes. Editor agent now filters editToolResults to only include entries containing 'successfully' and 'Changes made:' before yielding set_output. Scope: .agents/base2/scout.ts, .agents/base2/editor.ts.

eli5.text: The Scout agent can now directly read files in the codebase using a new tool, and its instructions explicitly tell it not to offer code changes. The Editor agent now reports only the edits that actually succeeded, filtering out failed attempts before passing results along. If you watched Scout investigate something, you'd see it open and inspect files on its own; if you watched the Editor, you'd see it only count the edits that completed successfully. The change is live in the internal tool set as of 2025-08-23.
